title: Replace repeated host object expansion with segmented array construction

source.title: vLLM PR #55469 and RTX 4060 reproduction
source.claim_scope: Transfer primitive derived from vLLM metadata construction; source speedups are not target evidence.

implementation_recipe: Express total output length as a reduction over per-segment counts.
Construct segment ids by repeating row ids according to counts.
Construct local offsets as global indices minus repeated exclusive prefix starts.
Convert to the required pinned dtype once, then retain the existing H2D boundary.
validation_recipe: Compare every output exactly for empty, zero-length, irregular and very large segments.
Test every accepted input integer width and verify output dtype does not drift.
Benchmark small and large segment counts separately with interleaved samples.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Python object creation and per-segment dispatch should collapse.
Bulk allocation, memory bandwidth, pinned conversion and H2D copy should become dominant.
failure_modes: Vectorized setup is slower for tiny inputs.
Prefix arithmetic overflows before the final cast.
A NumPy conversion silently changes dtype or pinning behavior.
Uniform-shape specialization is incorrectly applied to irregular rows.
scope_limits: Useful only when the host loop or object expansion is material in the target profile.
Does not justify removing mandatory host-visible metadata or synchronization.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: Each segment independently appends the local integer range 0..count-1.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: segments and their flattened output intervals
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Repeat each exclusive prefix start by its segment count and subtract it from the global flattened index.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Cast once to the public metadata dtype and stage through the existing ownership boundary.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Bulk array primitives replace Python span proportional to the number of segments.
anti_patterns: one Python range object per segment
one device launch per metadata group
dtype conversion inside the segment loop

candidate_archetypes.name: exclusive-prefix segmented index construction
candidate_archetypes.template: Compute counts and exclusive starts in bulk; derive flattened local indices from global indices minus repeated starts.
